knowledge:
- key_parameters: test=Path to the test BAM file ;; control=Path to the matched control BAM file ;; regions=GRanges or data.frame specifying genomic regions to analyze ;; q=Minimum base quality threshold for filtering reads ;; rho=Dispersion parameter for the beta-binomial model (e.g., 1e-4) ;; model=Model type for bbb, either "OR" or "AND" ;; alternative=Alternative hypothesis for estimateDispersion ("two.sided", "greater", "less") ;; combine.method=Method to combine p-values from forward and reverse strands (e.g., "fisher")
- alternatives: ShearwaterML (betabinLRT) vs original Shearwater (bbb). ShearwaterML is preferred when standard multiple testing correction (FDR control) is desired, as it yields p-values instead of Bayes factors. Original Shearwater (bbb) is preferred when incorporating prior information (e.g., COSMIC priors) to compute posterior probabilities.
- when_to_use: Use when calling low-frequency subclonal somatic mutations (SNVs) from deep sequencing data, either by comparing a single test sample to a matched control, or by analyzing a cohort of multiple samples to estimate background error rates.
- pitfalls: Analyzing raw, unnormalized data can lead to inflated p-values and false positives due to systematic sequencing biases; use normalize() to correct for this. Choosing an inappropriate dispersion parameter rho can bias variant calling; use estimateDispersion() to estimate it from the data.

workflows.name: pairwise_deepsnv
workflows.intent: Call subclonal single nucleotide variants by comparing a single test BAM file to a matched control BAM file.
input: test.bam (alignment file for the test/tumor sample)
control.bam (alignment file for the matched control/normal sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Define genomic regions of interest ;; 2. Run deepSNV to compare test and control BAM files ;; 3. Normalize the data to correct for systematic biases ;; 4. Estimate dispersion using a beta-binomial model ;; 5. Summarize significant SNVs
workflows.code:
regions <- data.frame(chr="B.FR.83.HXB2_LAI_IIIB_BRU_K034", start = 2074, stop=3585)

data("RCC", package="deepSNV")

workflows.name: shearwater_ml
workflows.intent: Call subclonal mutations across multiple BAM files using the Shearwater ML maximum-likelihood algorithm and output a VCF file.
input: files (vector of paths to BAM files)
workflows.stages: 1. Define genomic regions of interest ;; 2. Load count data from BAM files ;; 3. Compute p-values using the beta-binomial Likelihood Ratio Test ;; 4. Adjust p-values for multiple testing ;; 5. Convert results to VCF format
workflows.code:
regions <- GRanges("B.FR.83.HXB2_LAI_IIIB_BRU_K034", IRanges(start = 3120, end=3140))
files <- c(system.file("extdata", "test.bam", package="deepSNV"), system.file("extdata", "control.bam", package="deepSNV"))
counts <- loadAllData(files, regions, q=30)
pvals <- betabinLRT(counts, rho=1e-4, maxtruncate = 1)$pvals
qvals <- p.adjust(pvals, method="BH")
dim(qvals) = dim(pvals)
vcfML = qvals2Vcf(qvals, counts, regions, samples = files, mvcf = TRUE)

workflows.name: shearwater_bayes_factor
workflows.intent: Call subclonal mutations across multiple BAM files using the original Shearwater Bayes factor algorithm and output a VCF file.
input: files (vector of paths to BAM files)
workflows.stages: 1. Define genomic regions of interest ;; 2. Load count data from BAM files ;; 3. Compute Bayes factors ;; 4. Convert Bayes factors to VCF format
workflows.code:
regions <- GRanges("B.FR.83.HXB2_LAI_IIIB_BRU_K034", IRanges(start = 3120, end=3140))
files <- c(system.file("extdata", "test.bam", package="deepSNV"), system.file("extdata", "control.bam", package="deepSNV"))
counts <- loadAllData(files, regions, q=10)
bf <- bbb(counts, model = "OR", rho=1e-4)
vcf <- bf2Vcf(bf, counts, regions, cutoff = 0.5, samples = files, prior = 0.5, mvcf = TRUE)
